svg.title: Multiple sclerosis: a relapse is new neurological dysfunction lasting 24 hours or more with no other cause; the typical relapses are myelitis, optic neuritis and brainstem or cerebellar syndromes; the diagnosis needs dissemination in space and time on MRI, with CSF oligoclonal bands able to stand in for time, once better explanations are ruled out; treatment is disease-modifying therapy by category plus symptomatic therapy

svg.text: an immune attack (B and T cells) on central nervous system myelin → axonal damage, then loss

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: most common disabling neurological disease of young adults in Canada · women 3:1 · age 20-40

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: risk: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV, 32-fold) · adolescent obesity · smoking · low vitamin D or sunlight · shift work

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif
Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: NEW neurological symptoms · acute or subacute onset · lasting 24 HOURS or more · no other cause · not a pseudo-relapse

text.font-family: Arial, 'Segoe UI Symbol', 'Liberation Sans', Helvetica, sans-serif

svg.text: other features: sensory disturbances · fatigue · Lhermitte's sign (an electric shock down the back on bending the neck)

svg.text: spinal cord lesion · about 50% at onset
